newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Snecma set to buy out SEP.
newsitem.headline: France's Snecma set to buy out SEP.

text.p: The French government, belatedly attempting to consolidate a fragmented aerospace industry, Wednesday gave the green light for engine maker Snecma to buy up rocket engine manufacturer SEP.

State-owned Snecma already owns 51 percent of Societe Europeene de Propulsion (SEP) and wants to buy out minority shareholders to make it a wholly-owned subsidiary. The enlarged group would have annual sales of around 15 billion francs ($2.9 billion).
The deal has a strong industrial logic and would ensure Snecma's future in space programmes and its position as France's centre for engine manufacture, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.
SEP makes engines and boosters for Ariane rockets, used by the European Arianespace consortium.
Snecma makes civilian and military airplane engines including those for passenger jets of the Airbus Industrie consortium and Dassault Aviation combat planes.
